analysis_role: Post-result mechanistic falsification of the already-supported transition-regime H1. Test whether environmental tracking is bidirectionally reversible across U->D and D->U transition probabilities, rather than being carried only by one direction.

estimands.forward_alignment: Sum[P(U->D on edge) * dot(edge environmental shift, (+BIO15,-BIO1)/sqrt(2))] / Sum[P(U->D on edge)]
estimands.reverse_alignment: Sum[P(D->U on edge) * dot(edge environmental shift, (-BIO15,+BIO1)/sqrt(2))] / Sum[P(D->U on edge)]
estimands.bidirectional_floor: min(forward_alignment, reverse_alignment) within topology; primary statistic is median floor across the six accepted topologies

null: Enumerate all 126 count-preserving U/D assignments on the same nine taxa. Refit the symmetric CTMC rate for every state map and reuse the same Brownian environmental reconstructions and six accepted topologies.

decision.bidirectional_reversible_regime_supporte: forward and reverse alignment are positive on all six topologies and exact one-sided rank of the median bidirectional floor is <=0.05
decision.u_to_d_specific_asymmetry: forward alignment is positive on all six topologies but reverse alignment fails positivity on at least one topology
decision.bidirectional_directional_but_not_except: both directions are positive on all six topologies but exact floor rank is >0.05

claim_boundary: This is a post-result directional decomposition of H1, not independent confirmation.
Bidirectional alignment would show reversible present-niche transition-regime tracking, not historical climatic causation or adaptation.
Failure of reverse alignment does not prove evolutionary irreversibility; it only rejects symmetric environmental tracking under the declared CTMC/Brownian estimator.
No new environmental axis, taxon, threshold, or mechanism is admitted after result inspection.
